result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend three explicit modes, give strong reasons against the timing-based gestures, and admit what modes cost. B handles wrong-mode risk better: it keeps Record off the grid entirely, makes each drag undoable as one unit, uses only one confirmation so people still read it, and keeps the selection when switching modes to cut down on switches. It also ties the modes to the operator's actual workflow (look, change, commit). A adds useful ideas, a show-time lock and a dim-room test plan, but its safeguards are slightly less concrete about separating Record from casual gestures. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend three explicit modes, a persistent indicator that doesn't rely on color alone, defaulting to Select, undo for Paint and a confirmation step for Record. A is a little more concrete: selection carries across modes, Record sits outside the grid so a grid touch can never record a cue, and it states the cost it accepts. B ties its reasoning a little more closely to the live show, with a show-time lock state and a test in a dim room that counts errors. These strengths roughly cancel out, so neither answer is clearly better.
